notes:
Background: refactorvelocity.dev builds an in-IDE copilot used by 350+ engineers across web and mobile teams. Goal is deterministic completions (small continuations, full function bodies) with streaming so editor shows keystrokes in <50ms. Primary ask: Dedicated capacity for peak developer hours (09:00-18:00 PST) with predictable throughput + burst policy (allow 2x baseline bursts for daily standups/ship days).

Recent call highlights:
- CTO (M. Alvarez): "Latency kills adoption — even small delays and flicker break the dev flow. If not sub-50ms it's a non-starter."
- Staff Eng (S. Lee): wants model pinning per release channel (stable/dev) + ability to rollback to smaller quantized variant during incidents.
- Security: requires SSO/SAML integration, KMS support for customer-managed keys, audit logs for all token-level calls, 1 year retention controls and option for NA-only residency.

POC specifics / Evaluation criteria:
- 30-day Dedicated trial: 2 reserved GPU nodes for baseline, + burst capacity policy to handle +100% short spikes during peak (10:00-11:00, 15:00-16:00 PST).
- Metrics: median latency (target <50ms for 90% developer completions), p95 latency (<120ms), token cost / 1M, error rate (timeout/retry), hallucination/regression score on curated prompt set (repo of 250 prompts).
- Functional: streaming partial tokens in <40ms first-byte, stable model version pinning, canary rollouts across 10%->50%->100%, KV cache for common prefixes across sessions.

Commercial / Legal notes:
- Rough ARR target: $120-250k/year depending on committed capacity. Procurement timeline: Q2 2026. Legal flagged standard data processing addendum and source-code snippet handling clause (need clarifications).

Next steps (short):
- Run Dedicated perf POC w/ Redwood SE (Arjun) week of 2026-03-17 — simulate 200 devs hitting copilot concurrently during peak patterns.
- Provide detailed pricing deck and burst policy SLAs (drive link above).
- Legal to provide SOC2 evidence + redlined DPA.

Stated quotes / remarks from POC: "If Redwood can guarantee <50ms during our peak window and provide version pinning + canary safety nets, we can move to a 12-month commit for Dedicated."
